scores.evidence: Every key for a card shares the Redis hash tag {card_token}, so a single Lua script can touch them all atomically in one cluster slot
scores.rationale: Technology claims (Redis cluster hash tags, idempotent ZADD semantics, LightGBM missing-value handling with ONNX parity checks, STIP behavior, at-least-once with dedup) are accurate and the real limits of each choice are stated; only trivial arithmetic slips (buffer duration, guardrail timing) exist with no design consequence.

scores.evidence: Score 100% of card authorisations inline with our own logic ... Non-goals (v1): Anti-money-laundering transaction monitoring
scores.rationale: Solves exactly the stated problem inline at authorization, resolves ambiguities with explicit defaults, scopes exclusions with reasons, and is credibly buildable by the assumed 5-person team in staged milestones.

scores.evidence: Rules and models reach the service as immutable, versioned artifacts in S3. Only pipelines write them
scores.rationale: Every data entity has a system of record and sole writer, the single feature definition is honored across serving, replay and rebuild, and consistency, identity and degradation are handled the same way everywhere with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: Changes the plan if: p99 > 50 ms or Redis CPU > 60% at 1,000 TPS (shard more, slim the Lua, or consider asynchronous counters
scores.rationale: The riskiest assumptions (latency, label history, auth contract) are tested in week-1–2 spikes with explicit change-course triggers, gates block promotion (feature parity ≥99.9%, ONNX parity), and validation continues in production via drills, reconciliation and matured-label reports.

scores.evidence: A4 The Authorization Service can give us a 100 ms timeout ... If < 50 ms: embed the decision logic as a library
scores.rationale: Fourteen assumptions each state impact-if-wrong and how/when confirmed, numbers are marked as estimates or [A#] defaults, and the plan names which answers would reshape the design.

scores.evidence: Redis slow or down: after 20 ms, skip it ... The response carries degraded=FEATURES and a metric fires.
scores.rationale: Covers duplicates, out-of-order/reversal events, stand-in traffic, partial Kafka loss with reconciliation, bad-rule blast radius via guardrails, insider tampering, probing and selection bias, each with concrete detection, containment and recovery.

scores.evidence: Runbooks written in M1–M2: decline spike, guardrail tripped, timeout rate, Redis rebuild, ruleset rollback, model rollback
scores.rationale: Domain-meaningful alerts with thresholds, blue/green deploys with timed rollback procedures, Flyway/additive-proto migrations, and ownership split across fraud platform, fraud ops and cards teams sized to the stated team.

scores.evidence: Total ≈ $2–4.5k/month, plus staging at about 40% of that ... Cost is deliberately not a top driver
scores.rationale: Run costs are itemized as ranges with instance-level basis, controls (budget alert, lifecycle rules, query limits) are concrete, scaling behavior is noted (A11), and build-vs-buy trade-offs are reasoned in D0.

scores.evidence: The vendor contract (if any) is cancelled no earlier than 90 days after model enforcement. That cancellation is the only real point of no return.
scores.rationale: Every decision carries a reversibility rating and revisit trigger, the hard-to-reverse ones (auth-path contract, no-PAN contract, language) get early spikes, and exit paths (embed as library, swap Kinesis) are explicit.

scores.evidence: There is no stream processor in v1 ... Flink adds lag and a second hard-to-run system.
scores.rationale: Starts with the simplest workable design (one service, Redis, Kafka), defers Flink, UI, case management and multi-region each behind an explicit trigger, while keeping all essentials for the domain.

scores.evidence: T1 File long-lead requests: 24 months of historical auths + chargeback/dispute data ... Every ticket has a named owner and a committed date
scores.rationale: A dependency-ordered task breakdown with lanes, done-when criteria and spike-driven 'changes the plan if' branches lets a team start today without redoing the thinking.

checklist.evidence: p99 ≤ 50 ms server-side at 1,000 TPS sustained. ≥ 99.95% of authorisations answered before the 100 ms caller timeout
If we time out, **fail open** to the processor's existing stand-in rules.
Compute velocity features inside the request with **one atomic Redis call** ... replaying history through the same feature code the live service uses
The most recent 90 days are excluded from training because their labels haven't matured.
Value detection rate (fraud $ declined or alerted ÷ all fraud $) ≥ baseline + 30% at a false-positive ratio ≤ 10:1
action (APPROVE | DECLINE | APPROVE_ALERT | DECLINE_ALERT) ... Moving a rule from shadow to enforce is a one-line PR.
A reply of NO writes a fraud label and opens a case asking an analyst to block the card.
PAN: **never present**. The request contract has no PAN field, and a CI check plus a log scrubber reject 13–19-digit strings
a ZADD for a retried auth_id changes nothing, and a duplicate never double-counts ... Reversals feed a reversals_24h counter
daily population stability index on the top 20 features and on the score ... at least 2 weeks as challenger on live traffic
DecisionEvent contains the full request, every feature value used, the outcome of every rule (shadow and enforced), champion and challenger scores
At least 3 instances across 3 AZs ... designed and tested to 1,000 TPS sustained and 2,000 TPS burst

traps.evidence: Score inline, synchronously called by the Authorization Service ... Asynchronous-only catches fraud after the money is gone.
The Authorization Service times out at 100 ms and fails open to its own checks plus processor rules.
trains LightGBM with a time-based split. The most recent 90 days are excluded from training because their labels haven't matured.
The Decision Service, the Velocity Updater and the Replay Harness all use it. This is the main defence against the gap between training-time and serving-time features.
Use card tokens only, never the PAN (full card number), to keep PCI scope small.

note: An exemplary plan: technically precise, risk-ordered, proportionate and immediately actionable, avoiding every domain trap with explicit assumptions, early spikes and concrete rollback paths; weaknesses are limited to trivial arithmetic slips and a deferred rather than tiered fail-open policy.
